title: PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies

topic.reason: Forschungsergebnisse zu KI und Sprachmodellen (Treffer: we present, this paper, memory)

summary: Timing measurements are a fundamental building block of microarchitectural attacks, enabling software to convert otherwise invisible latency differences into architectural observations. Thus, restricting high-resolution timers is a common defense, especially in constrained environments such as web browsers. Timerless probing primitives provide an alternative approach. Instead of reading or constructing a timer, they observe architectural events that correlate with the microarchitectural state. However, such primitives typically rely on platform-specific behavior, and none generalizes across the wider computing landscape. In this paper, we present PhotoFinish, a portable timerless probing primitive that converts latency differences directly into an architectural value. PhotoFinish races an operation under test against a fixed reference in two parallel threads that then write unique values to the same shared location, resulting in a latency-dependent architectural value. PhotoFinish only requires parallel execution and shared memory, without constructing or reading a clock. We evaluate PhotoFinish on 38 CPUs spanning four ISAs and demonstrate reliable cache state classification acros
